s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of upper gastrointestinal bleeding with epigastric pain
salient_findings: Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration
key_facts: One-week history of epigastric pain and hematemesis
No significant medical or surgical history
Hemoglobin rose to 10 g/dL after transfusion
Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa
Well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa, consistent with GIST presentation

shortlist.label: Peptic ulcer disease
shortlist.why_kept: Epigastric pain and hematemesis, with a history of smoking, which is a risk factor for peptic ulcers

shortlist.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding and a mass in the pre-pyloric region, although biopsy showed no malignant features, cancer cannot be entirely ruled out

shortlist.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of upper gastrointestinal bleeding with a submucosal lesion, which could be consistent with a Dieulafoy's lesion

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation, which could be consistent with a lipoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation on CT is most consistent with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor, especially given the lack of malignant features on biopsy which might have suggested gastric adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Peptic ulcer disease
rejected.why: While peptic ulcer disease could cause epigastric pain and hematemesis, the presence of a submucosal lesion and a well-defined mass is not typical for peptic ulcers.

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy showed no malignant features, making gastric adenocarcinoma less likely.

rejected.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
rejected.why: Dieulafoy's lesion typically presents with a small, bleeding mucosal defect over a large, tortuous artery, which does not match the description of a submucosal lesion with a well-defined mass.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: While lipomas can be submucosal and have fat attenuation on CT, they are typically not associated with ulceration of the overlying mucosa or significant bleeding as seen in this patient.
